Obliterate

/uh-BLIT-uh-rayt/ - the stress falls on BLIT · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Obliterate means to destroy completely, leaving no trace.

Three laser sessions obliterated the tattoo, and the skin healed so evenly the artist could not say where it had been.

Worked Example

Nine villages around Verdun were shelled so thoroughly in 1916 that when the war ended there was nothing to rebuild — no walls, no wells, not a street line traceable under the leaf litter. France never rebuilt them. Each site keeps a signboard in the forest, naming a town that exists now only as a name.

Obliterate is the exact word for what the shelling did, because it means to destroy completely, leaving no trace — and the no trace clause is the whole word. The Latin beneath it meant to blot out the letters: erasure so total the page forgets the ink. Damage leaves wreckage to point at; even demolish leaves rubble. Obliterate leaves absence.

How Obliterate Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

erase

erase: to remove a mark; obliterate insists that no trace at all survives

blot out

blot out: to cover or wipe until it cannot be seen — the old ink-and-letters picture

Antonyms

restore

restore: to bring it back to what it was

conserve

conserve: to keep it intact for the future

How Strong Is It? — smudge → erase → obliterate

smudge vs. obliterate

smudge vs. obliterate: Smudge is the smallest step — the mark blurs, but anyone can see something was there.

erase vs. obliterate

erase vs. obliterate: Erase goes further than smudge — the mark itself comes off the page — but obliterate claims the most: nothing left to show anything was ever there.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — ob-

Prefix — ob-: over, against

Root — liter

Root — liter: letter (Latin littera)

Suffix — -ate

Suffix — -ate: verb ending

Put it together

Put it together: Ob- (over) + liter (letter) + -ate = to draw over the letters. A Roman scribe obliterating a wax tablet smeared it until no stroke survived — and the word still demands that much: not damaged, not merely faded, but gone without residue.

Use the root in a new word: literacy

Use the root in a new word: literacy: The one-room school pushed literacy above all else: every farm child reading by eight and writing by nine.

Root Check

Word Choice

emphatic / formal

Obliterate is the totality word: reach for it only when nothing is left to point at. Its unit-mates divide destruction's labor — raze levels a building but leaves the rubble and the lot; eradicate wipes out something living or spreading, to the last case; obliterate erases even the last signs. If a trace survives, the word has been overspent.
